To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) parallel fiber feedback can switch between enhancement and suppression, 2) this switching is mediated by non monotonic firing rate response of the postsynaptic neurons, 3) the non monotonic firing is a result of a shift from a balanced state to a state of dominant inhibition, and 4) the non monotonical response provides the basis for a simple negative image generation.

the non monotonic firing of pyramidal cells in response to parallel fiber inputs can be explained by the interaction of direct excitation and inhibition and that this non monotoncity provides a simple mechanism for the cancellation of reafference in the ELL.

parallel fiber feedback onto ELL pyramids is a dynamic system that can switch between enhancement and cancellation of sensory inputs, and this switching is mediated through a non monotonic response to parallel fiber activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the control of neuronal firing by parallel fiber feedback.
understanding the dynamics of parallel fiber feedback and how these dynamics shape the synaptic inputs onto pyramidal cells in ELL.
the role of feedback in the processing of self generated inputs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dynamic interaction of multiple parallel fiber inputs onto pyramidal cells in ELL provides the neural substrate for negative image generation, which in turn is a mechanism that can suppress reafference.
the dynamic parallel fiber feedback onto ELL pyramidals provides a simple mechanism for negative image generation that can be tuned by changes in the mean rate of parallel fibers.

parallel fiber feedback provides a mechanism for the cancellation of self generated sensory inputs, which involves the generation of a non monotonic input output function, and the dynamic modulation of this function by changes in the firing rate of the parallel fiber inputs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamics of parallel fiber feedback, in conjunction with the dynamics of the pyramidal cell membrane potential, can generate a negative image of sensory inputs.
the non monotonic firing rate response of ELL pyramoidal neurons to parallel fiber inputs provides the basis for the generation of a cancellation signal through anti Hebbiann plasticity.

the non monotonicity of the response to parallel fiber feedback, combined with the ability of this pathway to change its mean activity, provides a simple basis by which parallel fiber feedback can generate a negative image of sensory inputs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dynamic interaction between parallel fibers and pyramidal neurons provides a simple mechanism for the generation of a cancellation mechanism that is independent of the precise timing of the feedback.
dynamic feedback pathways can shape sensory inputs in complex ways, and that this shaping is not necessarily limited to the generation of a simple negative image.
parallel fiber feedback is capable of controlling the firing response of pyramidal neurons through a combination of direct excitation, inhibition and anti Hebbian synaptic plasticity.
